data.description:
## Symptom

Running plan review through the MCP server (`review_plan_start` / `review_plan`) can
review a **stale copy of the ticket description** instead of the current one. After
editing a ticket's description to address blocking findings, a fresh MCP review returned
**byte-identical findings** -- including findings whose text had already been removed
from the plan -- and recorded a `material_parts.description` fingerprint matching the
pre-edit description rather than the edited one.

Running `rebar review-plan <id>` from a local worktree immediately afterwards, with no
other change, read the current description and produced different (correct) findings.

## Why this is serious

Plan review is a **gate that mints a signed attestation**, and the attestation's whole
value is that it binds a verdict to specific pinned material. If the material the MCP
path pins is not the material in the store, then:

- A plan can be BLOCKED for findings the author has already fixed, with no way to clear
  them through the MCP path -- the author edits, re-reviews, and gets the same verdict.
- More dangerously, the inverse: a plan can be PASSED and certified against a description
  that is no longer what the ticket says.

`AGENTS.md` instructs agents to route tracker operations, explicitly including
`review-plan`, through the MCP server when one is configured. So the documented default
path is the affected one, and the working path (local CLI) is documented as the fallback.

## Evidence

Observed in session `cd818479-c2e0-4a67-a07f-2d230e321466` on more than one ticket. The
tell is the `material_fingerprint` / `material_parts.description` in the review result:
compare it against a fingerprint computed from the description that `show_ticket` returns
at the same moment. When they disagree, the review ran on stale material.

## What is NOT yet known

Where the staleness is introduced. Candidates, in rough order of suspicion:

- The MCP server holds a long-lived store handle or compiled-state cache that is not
  invalidated when a description-edit event arrives from another writer.
- The MCP server's checkout of the tickets branch is refreshed on a poll interval rather
  than on read.
- A de-duplication layer (`REBAR_MCP_DEDUP`) attaching a new request to an in-flight or
  recently-completed run keyed in a way that ignores the description having changed.

The third is worth ruling in or out early, because byte-identical findings are exactly
what an unintended cache hit looks like.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The root cause is identified with evidence, not inference; the staleness window is
      characterized (what invalidates it, and how long it persists).
- [ ] A reproduction exists: edit a description, immediately request a review over MCP,
      and show the reviewed material matching the edit.
- [ ] Plan review over MCP pins the same description bytes that `show_ticket` returns at
      the same moment, and a regression test asserts that equality.
- [ ] If a cache or de-dup key is implicated, it incorporates the material fingerprint so
      a changed description cannot hit a prior entry.
- [ ] No signed attestation can be produced against material that differs from the
      stored ticket at review time.
data.title: MCP plan-review can review and attest against a stale ticket description
